strings.name: Shirin Ebadi
strings.summary: A former Iranian judge, Ebadi was removed from judging after the 1979 revolution and later represented women, children and political dissidents as a lawyer. She won the 2003 Nobel Peace Prize and co-founded the Nobel Women’s Initiative. In exile since 2009, she continues criticizing Iran’s rights record and in 2026 joined transitional-justice drafting announced by exiled opposition figures.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; reviewed on 15 November. This is not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: As a lawyer and judge long advanced women’s, children’s and political rights, won the Nobel Peace Prize and conducts international advocacy.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Hamadan, Iran, born in 1947; sources differ on the precise birthday.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Law studies at the University of Tehran, graduating in 1968, followed by judicial training.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Human-rights law
strings.highlights.h1.text: Represented rights cases and co-founded the Defenders of Human Rights Center, protecting women’s, children’s and political rights; received the 2003 peace prize.
strings.highlights.h2.title: International women’s cooperation
strings.highlights.h2.text: Co-founded the Nobel Women’s Initiative with fellow laureates and continued advocacy in exile.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Joined transitional-justice drafting
strings.timeline.t1.text: Reza Pahlavi announced her participation in a drafting committee, an exile-opposition initiative rather than an Iranian state court.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Began exile
strings.timeline.t2.text: Remained abroad after the presidential election and continued human-rights advocacy.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Co-founded women’s initiative
strings.timeline.t3.text: Established a joint initiative with fellow women peace laureates.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Won Nobel Peace Prize
strings.timeline.t4.text: Recognized for democracy and human rights, especially women and children.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Licensed as a lawyer
strings.timeline.t5.text: Opened private practice after obtaining her licence, representing rights cases.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Removed from judging
strings.timeline.t6.text: Women judges were removed after the revolution; she was assigned clerical duties.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Presided over Tehran court branch
strings.timeline.t7.text: Became president of a Tehran City Court branch.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Began judicial career
strings.timeline.t8.text: Entered the judiciary after legal education and judicial training.
